abstract: Kinsta is premium managed WordPress hosting with top-tier speed and human support. It starts at $35 a month, and the Black Friday offer saves about 12.5% over the first year.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes for sites where speed and support matter. Webhostingcat measured a 100% GTmetrix score, and WP Umbrella recorded 100% uptime on its monitored sites.
It is worth it for agencies, WooCommerce stores and busy sites. WP Umbrella says it is not the right fit for small sites with little traffic.
Launch is $35 a month at list price. Agency plans run from $340 to $675 a month, and Enterprise starts at $500.

mainEntity.name: What is the Kinsta Black Friday offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: 50% off for 3 months on monthly plans, or 3 months free with annual billing, for new customers. It ends on 1 December 2026.
No. Support is 24/7 through chat and tickets, with human help in 8 languages listed.
Yes. WP Umbrella hosts WooCommerce stores on it, and Webhostingcat's load test finished 1,000 requests with no timeouts.
Yes. Kinsta lists free site migrations, and WP Umbrella says the team moved sites from other hosts without help.

mainEntity.name: Does Kinsta include email or domains?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Kinsta does one thing: managed WordPress and WooCommerce hosting.
We found no built-in AI assistant. It has an API and tutorials for building your own MCP server.
Kinsta is fully managed and costs more. Cloudways costs less and gives more control. Hostingstep measured similar response times for the two.

mainEntity.name: Does Kinsta have a money-back guarantee?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Kinsta lists a 30-day money-back guarantee.
Owners of small, low-traffic sites on a tight budget, and anyone who wants phone support or email in the same account.
